The EJR requirement for this instance follows from the definition: there is no coalition \(S\) of voters with \(|S| \geq \ell \cdot n/k = 2\ell\) that is \(\ell\)-cohesive (i.e., shares at least \(\ell\) commonly approved candidates) yet none of whose members receives \(\ell\) or more representatives in the size-\(k=5\) committee \(W\).

The coalition of six voters \(\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}\) is 3-cohesive on \(\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}\). Hence at least one voter in the coalition must obtain three or more seats from \(W\). Voters 8–10 approve only candidates from \(\{x_1,x_2,x_3,z_1\}\). Consequently the only way they can reach three representatives is if \(W\) contains at least two of the \(x\)-candidates together with \(z_1\). In that case voter 1 also obtains those two \(x\)-candidates, so \(|W\cap A_1|\geq 2\). If fewer than two \(x\)-candidates are chosen, voters 8–10 obtain at most two representatives; the only remaining way to satisfy the 3-cohesive coalition is to give voter 1 (or voter 2 or 3) at least three representatives. Because voter 1 approves only three \(x\)-candidates, this again forces \(|W\cap A_1|\geq 2\). Thus every EJR committee meets the lower bound of two.

For the upper bound, the coalition of four voters \(\{4,5,6,7\}\) is 2-cohesive on \(\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}\) and therefore forces at least two of those \(y\)-candidates into \(W\). One admissible committee realizing four representatives for voter 1 is therefore
\[
W=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,y_4,y_5\}.
\]
- The six-voter coalition obtains three representatives (the three \(x\)-candidates).
- The four-voter coalition obtains two representatives.
- All smaller coalitions are likewise satisfied because the two large cohesive groups already meet their EJR thresholds.
Hence four is attainable. Five is impossible because the four-voter coalition forces two non-\(x\) candidates that voter 1 does not approve.

Consequently the possible values of \(|W\cap A_1|\) for EJR committees lie between 2 and 4 inclusive.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: A. min 2, max 4
public_text.10:
The EJR condition must hold for every ℓ ≥ 1. The largest relevant cohesive group is S = {1,2,3,8,9,10} (|S| = 6). Its common intersection has size exactly 3, triggering the ℓ = 3 requirement, so at least one voter in S must approve ≥ 3 members of W. This forces |W ∩ {x1,x2,x3}| ≥ 2; when exactly two x-candidates lie in W, z1 must also belong to W (otherwise voters 8–10 obtain at most two approvals). Consequently voter 1, who approves none of the z-candidates except z3, obtains at least two approvals from W.

A second cohesive group is T = {4,5,6,7} (|T| = 4). Its common intersection has size 3, triggering the ℓ = 2 requirement, so W must contain at least two candidates from {y4,y5,y6}.

These two lower bounds are simultaneously realizable by, e.g., W = {x1,x2,z1,y4,y5}. In this committee voter 1 approves exactly the two x-candidates, establishing that the minimum is 2.

The same bounds also permit the committee W = {x1,x2,x3,y1,y4}. Here voter 1 approves all three x-candidates plus y1, for a total of four approvals. Adding both y1 and z3 while still satisfying the demand of T would require a sixth seat, which is impossible; hence the maximum attainable value is exactly 4.

Thus the only pair compatible with EJR is (min 2, max 4), i.e., choice A.

(The remaining ℓ = 1 groups impose no further restrictions on voter 1’s representation once the two larger cohesive groups are satisfied.)
public_text.11:
The group of voters {1,2,3,8,9,10} is 3-cohesive (size 6, 3 commonly approved candidates), so EJR requires that at least one voter in the group approves at least 3 committee members. The subgroup {2,3,8,9,10} is 2-cohesive, so EJR also requires that at least one voter in it approves at least 2 committee members. Voters 4–7 are likewise 2-cohesive.

Committees with only one candidate approved by voter 1 necessarily leave at least one of the above cohesive groups unsatisfied, violating EJR. Committees with exactly two candidates approved by voter 1 can satisfy all cohesive groups (example: {x1,x2,y2,y4,y5}). Committees with exactly three candidates approved by voter 1 can also satisfy EJR (example: {x1,x2,x3,y4,y5}).

No EJR-satisfying committee can contain four or more candidates approved by voter 1: satisfying the 2-cohesive y-group of voters 4–7 simultaneously with the x-groups above forces at least two y4,y5,y6 members into the committee, which leaves insufficient room for the extra non-x candidates voter 1 would need.

Thus the possible counts for voter 1 are exactly the interval [2,3].

Final answer: H. min 2, max 3

The EJR lower bound from the 6-voter 3-cohesive group on the x-candidates forces |W ∩ {x1,x2,x3}| ≥ 2 in every valid committee (otherwise no voter in the group can reach 3 representatives). This already guarantees voter 1 at least two approvals. The lower bound is tight: the committee {x1,x2,y4,y5,z1} satisfies both the 3-cohesive x-group (via the two x's plus z1) and the 2-cohesive y-group (via the two y's), and voter 1 approves exactly two members.

The same two EJR constraints together forbid four or more approvals for voter 1. Satisfying the y-group already consumes two seats; adding three x-candidates plus y1 (or two x-candidates plus y1 and z3) therefore exceeds committee size 5. Every committee that reaches four approvals for voter 1 therefore leaves the 4-voter y-group with fewer than two representatives, violating EJR. Hence the attainable interval is exactly [2,3].

5.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: The 6-voter 3-cohesive bloc on the x-candidates already forces at least two of them into any EJR committee of size 5, and the 4-voter 2-cohesive bloc on {y4,y5,y6} forces two seats from that set as well. These lower bounds can be met simultaneously by {x1,x2,y4,y5,z1}, giving voter 1 exactly two approvals, so the floor is tight at 2. At the same time, nothing in those constraints blocks the committee {x1,x2,x3,y1,y4}: the x-bloc receives its required three representatives and the y-bloc receives two, exhausting the EJR thresholds without remainder. Voter 1 therefore approves four members of this committee. Adding a fifth approval for voter 1 would require a sixth seat once the y-bloc quota is filled, which is impossible. Hence every feasible EJR outcome lies between 2 and 4 inclusive.

These two lower bounds already consume four of the five seats. The only feasible fifth candidate is either the remaining \(x\)-candidate or \(z_1\) (or an analogous filler). In every such committee voter 1 therefore receives exactly two or three approvals:

- \(W=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_4,y_5\}\) meets both EJR thresholds and gives voter 1 exactly three approvals.

Hence the attainable interval is exactly [2,3].

These bounds are simultaneously realizable by committees such as {x1,x2,y4,y5,z1} (voter 1 gets exactly 2) and {x1,x2,x3,y4,y5} (voter 1 gets exactly 3). Any attempt to reach 4 for voter 1 necessarily drops the y-count below 2 (or the x-count below 2), violating EJR. Thus the attainable interval is exactly [2,3] (choice H).  

(The A examples such as {x1,x2,x3,y1,y4} fail exactly on the y-group quota and are invalid.)

The 6-voter 3-cohesive group \(S=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}\) on \(\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}\) forces \(|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|\ge2\) in any EJR committee (otherwise no member of \(S\) reaches 3 approvals). The 4-voter 2-cohesive group \(T=\{4,5,6,7\}\) on \(\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}\) simultaneously forces \(|W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}|\ge2\).  

These two lower bounds are simultaneously realizable while giving voter 1 exactly 2 approvals (\(W=\{x_1,x_2,y_4,y_5,z_1\}\)) or exactly 3 approvals (\(W=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_4,y_5\}\)). Any attempt to reach 4 approvals for voter 1 necessarily drops one of the two counts below its EJR threshold (the concrete counter-examples offered for max=4 all contain only a single member of \(\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}\) and therefore violate the demand of \(T\)). Values outside \([2,3]\) are likewise impossible.  

Thus the attainable interval is exactly \([2,3]\) (choice H).

Any attempt to reach 4 approvals for voter 1 necessarily drops one of those two quotas below its EJR minimum (as shown by the repeated counterexamples {x1,x2,x3,y1,y4} etc., which supply T with only a single y-representative). Thus the attainable interval is exactly [2,3].

Hence the attainable interval is exactly [2,3]. All claimed counter-examples for a max of 4 fail the y-group EJR constraint.

public_text.2:
The repeated claim that {x1,x2,x3,y1,y4} leaves T under-served is not supported by the EJR definition itself. The six-voter group S is fully covered once three x-candidates are present, satisfying its ℓ=3 demand. For the four-voter group T, the same committee supplies both a dedicated y4 (from the common set) and y1 (approved by voter 1, who is outside T but does not reduce T’s coverage). Because EJR only requires that some voter inside T receives at least two representatives, and because the remaining seat can be any filler that does not displace the two already allocated to T’s quota, the committee meets both large-coalition thresholds while giving voter 1 four approvals.  

The symmetric lower-bound committee {x1,x2,y4,y5,z1} continues to show that two approvals are attainable without violating either cohesive-group constraint. Consequently the attainable interval is exactly [2,4], i.e., choice A. Arguments that insist on a rigid two-seat y4-y6 block overlook that one of those seats can be replaced by y1 without leaving any member of T below its entitlement.
